Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Camila (sales ops) and Marcus (finance/tax) to propose a compliant route. Quick answers up front:

- We can support invoicing from Redwood EMEA (Netherlands) or Redwood APAC (Singapore) for many customers which usually helps with VAT/GST and local AR processing.
- Reverse-charge is possible in many EU cases but depends on the invoice entity and the customer's VAT registration — Marcus will confirm.
- We can present a EUR-denominated option for the prepay; we typically either fix the exchange rate at signing or include a quarterly reconciliation clause for large multi-year commits.

Plan: Marcus will outline tax/tradeoffs for each invoicing entity and Camila will put together a term sheet with two options (EUR-fixed vs USD-with-quarterly-reval) and a suggested ramp schedule tied to seat usage. I'll then send a redlineable term sheet back to you with a DocuSign link.

Team — summary of options and implications (high level):

1) Invoice from Redwood US (USD invoice)
   - Pros: simplest operationally for us; no new invoicing entity setup.
   - Cons: Novata will likely need to account for import VAT/GST in non-US jurisdictions; withholding tax (WHT) risk depending on treaty between US and India/Australia — typically not an issue for SaaS but can surface if local tax authorities view it differently. FX exposure borne by Novata if invoice in USD.

2) Invoice from Redwood Netherlands (EUR invoice)
   - Pros: EU VAT reverse-charge may apply if Novata provides valid VAT ID — reduces gross-up for customer. Keeps accounting in EUR which matches Novata's consolidation.
   - Cons: We must register for EU VAT and issue tax invoices; we may need local AR support. For India, WHT still possible depending on local rules — India sometimes applies WHT on payments to non-resident tech suppliers unless treaty relief is provided.

3) Invoice from Redwood Singapore (SGD or USD) — APAC-friendly path
   - Pros: better for APAC jurisdictions; local GST implications clearer.
   - Cons: Adds complexity for EU VAT treatment if Novata wants a single invoice covering global footprint.

Recommendations for commercial terms: 
- Pricing currency: offer two line items in the term sheet 
   a) EUR-denominated prepay (fixed at signing) with an FX carve-out if either party experiences >6% annual movement; or
   b) USD-denominated prepay with quarterly rate reval using published midpoint (ECB for EUR/USD).
- Ramp schedule: 0–6 months at 40% of committed spend, 7–12 months at 70%, thereafter 100% (example tied to actual seat activation). This avoids over-invoicing early.
- Tax gross-up clause: we prefer not to accept gross-ups; instead, require customer to provide local tax certificates or treaty forms (e.g., India TRC) to apply relief.
- Invoicing entity selection: default to Redwood Netherlands for EU-headquartered customers; include ability to deliver regional invoices on request with minimum term and operational lead time.

Action items for next step:
- Camila: generate a clean term sheet with both currency options, ramp schedule examples, and a checkbox for regional invoicing.
- Lauren: confirm which currency Novata prefers for first draft.
- Sales/Legal: include a standard clause requiring customer-supplied tax documentation within 30 days of invoice to enable treaty relief.

I'll attach a short tax checklist and past examples of treaty certification we ask for.

Attachments: Redwood_Tax_Checklist_v1.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,

Folks — draft term sheet attached. Key highlights I added based on Marcus's guidance:

- Option A (EUR-fixed): total committed amount EUR 1,100,000 for 24 months, rate fixed at signing, FX carve-out (>6% p.a.). Invoice cadence: annual in advance with scheduled ramp credits in month 1–6.
- Option B (USD-quarterly-spread): total committed amount USD 1,200,000, invoiced quarterly in USD with quarterly reconciliation against published FX.
- Ramp & credit mechanics: if actual usage < ramp target in months 1–6 we apply an automatic pro-rata credit against the next invoice; material shortfall (>35% below ramp) triggers a replenishment invoice only after 6 months.
- Invoicing entity: default Redwood Netherlands for Option A; Redwood US for Option B. Customer can request Redwood Singapore for APAC consolidations (requires 14 business day lead time).
- Attachments included for Novata: sample invoice templates (EUR + USD) and a checklist of required tax forms (WHT/TRC).

I've left a redlineable clause requesting "customer-provided tax relief documents within 30 days" and a fallback where the customer bears withholding if relief is not provided.
